chunks: ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī narrated from Abī Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Riḍā عليه السلام, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

I heard my father Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام saying: “ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd al-Baṣrī entered upon Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. When he greeted him and sat down, he recited this verse: ‘Those who avoid the major sins,’ then he stopped. So Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: ‘What made you stop?’ He said: ‘I would like to know the major sins from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.’ He said: ‘Yes, O ʿAmr.’”
“The greatest of the major sins is shirk with Allah. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says:”
“Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him.”
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allah, then Allah has forbidden Jannah for him, and his refuge is the Fire, and the wrongdoers have no helpers.”
And after it is despair of the mercy of Allah, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“Indeed, none despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelieving people.”
Then feeling secure from the plan of Allah, because Allah, Exalted, says:
“None feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.”
And among them is disobedience to parents, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the disobedient one arrogant and wretched in His saying, Exalted is He:
“And dutiful to my mother, and He did not make me arrogant and wretched.”
And killing the soul which Allah, Exalted, has forbidden except with right, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Jahannam, abiding in it.”
To the end of the verse. And accusing chaste women, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unaware, believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment.”
And consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly, due to the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly only consume fire into their bellies, and they shall enter a Blaze.”
And fleeing from the battlefield, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“And whoever turns his back to them on that day, unless maneuvering for battle or joining another group, has incurred wrath from Allah, and his refuge is Jahannam, and evil is the destination.”
And consuming riba, because Allah, Exalted, says:
“Those who consume riba do not stand except as one stands whom Shaytan has confounded by touch.”
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“O you who believe, have taqwa of Allah and leave what remains of riba, if you are believers. But if you do not, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger.”
And sorcery, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“And they certainly knew that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter.”
And zina, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“And whoever does that shall meet a penalty. The punishment will be multiplied for him on the Day of Qiyamah, and he shall abide therein humiliated, except one who repents and believes.”
The verse. And the engulfing false oath, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price, those shall have no share in the Hereafter.”
The verse. And misappropriation; Allah, Exalted, said:
“And whoever misappropriates will bring what he misappropriated on the Day of Qiyamah.”
And withholding the obligatory zakat, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Jahannam and their foreheads, sides, and backs will be branded with it: this is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard.”
And false testimony and concealing testimony, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“And whoever conceals it, then his heart is sinful.”

And drinking khamr, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has equated it with the worship of idols. And deliberately abandoning salat, or anything from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory, because the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘Whoever abandons salat deliberately has dissociated himself from the covenant of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the covenant of His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله.’ And breaking the covenant and severing kinship ties, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
“Those — for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode.”
He said: Then ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd went out, crying aloud from his weeping, saying: ‘Perished is the one who speaks by his own opinion and disputes with you concerning virtue and knowledge.’

key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury or unlawful increase in financial dealings
key_terms.الزِّكاةِ الْمَفْرُوضَةِ: the obligatory zakat that must be given
key_terms.الْكَبَائِرِ: the major sins, grave acts for which severe divine warning is given
key_terms.عُقُوقُ الْوَالِدَيْنِ: disobedience and undutiful conduct toward one's parents

ai.seo_question: What are the major sins in the Qur'an according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a Qur'an-based enumeration of major sins as taught by Imam Abu ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, beginning with shirk and extending to moral, financial, familial, and devotional violations. It emphasizes that the gravity of these sins is known through explicit divine threats in the Qur'an and Prophetic teaching. The report closes by showing the spiritual impact of the Imam’s knowledge on ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4932 - Abdul-Azim ibn Abdullah al-Hasani narrated from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Ridha (as), from his father (as), who said: 
I heard my father Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) say:
'Amr ibn 'Ubayd al-Basri entered upon Abu Abdullah (as). When he greeted him and sat down, he recited the verse: "Those who avoid the major sins" (Surah Al-Shura 42:37), then he stopped.
Imam (as) said to him: "What has made you stop?"
He replied: "I wish to know the major sins from the Book of Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic."
Imam (as) said: "Yes, O 'Amr, 
the greatest of the major sins is associating partners with Allah (swt).
Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating partners with Him' (Surah An-Nisa 4:48).
And Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allah, then Allah has forbidden Paradise for him, and his abode is the Fire, and there are no helpers for the wrongdoers' (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:72).
After that is despairing of the mercy of Allah (swt) - for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'Indeed, no one despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelieving people' (Surah Yusuf 12:87).
Then, feeling secure from the plan of Allah (swt), for Allah (swt), the Exalted, says:
'None feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people' (Surah Al-A'raf 7:99).
Among them is disobedience to parents, for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, has made the disobedient one arrogant and wretched, as He (swt) says in His (swt) Book:
'And dutiful to my mother, and He did not make me an arrogant wretched one' (Surah Maryam 19:32)."
And the killing of a soul 'which Allah has forbidden, except by right' (Surah Al-Isra 17:33), for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally...' (Surah An-Nisa 4:93) until the end of the verse.
And accusing chaste women, for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unaware, believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment' (Surah An-Nur 24:23).
And consuming the wealth of the orphan unjustly, for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly are only filling their bellies with fire, and they will be burned in a Blaze' (Surah An-Nisa 4:10).
And fleeing from the battlefield, for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'And whoever turns his back to them on that day, unless maneuvering for battle or joining another company, has certainly drawn upon himself the wrath of Allah, and his refuge is Hell-and wretched is the destination' (Surah Al-Anfal 8:16).
And consuming usury, for Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: 
'Those who consume usury will not stand except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:275).
And Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains [due to you] of usury, if you should be believers. But if you do not, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger...' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:278-279).
And sorcery, for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'And they certainly knew that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter...' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:102).
And fornication, for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'And whoever does that shall meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated-except for those who repent and believe...' (Surah Al-Furqan 25:68-70).
And the false oath (al-yamin al-ghamus), for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price will have no share in the Hereafter...' (Surah Aal-e-Imran 3:77)
.
And misappropriation (ghulul), for Allah (swt), the Exalted, says: 
'And whoever misappropriates [an item], he will bring forth what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection...' (Surah Aal-e-Imran 3:161)."
And withholding the obligatory Zakat, for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell and their foreheads, their sides, and their backs will be branded with it: This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard' (Surah At-Tawbah 9:35).
And false testimony and concealing testimony, for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'And whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:283).
And drinking intoxicants, for Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, has equated it with the worship of idols.
And deliberately abandoning prayer or anything that Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, has made obligatory, for the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever deliberately abandons prayer has indeed removed himself from the protection of Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, and the protection of His Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him and his family).'
And breaking covenants and severing family ties (swt), for Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, says: 
'For them is the curse, and for them is the worst home' (Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:25).
Then 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd left, crying loudly and saying, 'Perished is the one who speaks based on his own opinion and disputes with you (Imam (as)) in virtue and knowledge!'"
